## Aim

This is a script that downloads the BrainSpan developmental transcriptome
(RNA-seq, Gencode v10, summarised to genes) from the NeMO archive and then
loads it into R. The data available comes as three files:

-   `expression_matrix.csv`: RPKM values, one row per gene and one column
    per sample. No header row, first column is a row number.
-   `rows_metadata.csv`: gene information (one row per gene).
-   `columns_metadata.csv`: sample information such as donor, age, sex
    and brain region (one row per sample).

The output is a file `data/01_dat_load.tsv`, and it combines all three into one 
table with one row per sample. It has sample information first, then one column 
per gene

Do note that the website from which the data is downloaded seems to have server
issues fairly frequently. If an error occurs during downloading, please check 
the server status and re-try when the website is up.

## Loading libraries

```{r}
#| message: false
library("tidyverse")
library("here")
library("curl")
source(file = here("R/99_proj_func.R"))
```

## Define data locations

```{r}
data_dir <- here("data")
raw_dir <- here("data/_raw")
base_url <- str_c("https://data.nemoarchive.org/other/grant/brainspan/",
                  "transcriptome/bulk/",
                  "RNAseqDevelopmentalTranscriptomeDataset/",
                  "RnaseqGencode_v10_SummarizedToGenes/")
raw_files <- c("expression_matrix.csv",
               "columns_metadata.csv",
               "rows_metadata.csv")
```
## Download data

The `data/` folder is not on GitHub as per assignment instructions, so after a 
fresh clone it does not exist.So we must create `data/` and `data/_raw/`, then 
we download each file only if it is missing.

```{r}
if (!dir.exists(data_dir)) {
  dir.create(path = data_dir)
}
if (!dir.exists(raw_dir)) {
  dir.create(path = raw_dir)
}

raw_files |>
  map(.f = ~ download_if_missing(file_name = .x,
                                 base_url = base_url,
                                 raw_dir = raw_dir))
```
## Read data

```{r}
#| message: false
columns_metadata <- read_csv(file = str_c(raw_dir, "/columns_metadata.csv"))

rows_metadata <- read_csv(file = str_c(raw_dir, "/rows_metadata.csv"))

# The matrix has no header row. With col_names = FALSE, readr names the
# columns X1, X2, X3, ... instead of using the first row of data as names
expression_matrix <- read_csv(file = str_c(raw_dir, "/expression_matrix.csv"),
                              col_names = FALSE)
```
## Check the loaded data

The matrix should have one row per gene in `rows_metadata`, and one
column per sample in `columns_metadata` plus the row number column.

```{r}
tibble(table = c("expression_matrix",
                 "rows_metadata",
                 "columns_metadata"),
       n_rows = c(nrow(expression_matrix),
                  nrow(rows_metadata),
                  nrow(columns_metadata)),
       n_cols = c(ncol(expression_matrix),
                  ncol(rows_metadata),
                  ncol(columns_metadata)))
```

Each Ensembl gene ID should appear only once, otherwise genes would be
merged when we make one column per gene.

```{r}
rows_metadata |>
  count(ensembl_gene_id) |>
  filter(n > 1)
```

## Combine into one table

We put the Data into table. Each gene column is named
`<ensembl_gene_id>_<gene_symbol>` so both identifiers are kept for
`02_clean.qmd`. Genes without a symbol keep only their Ensembl ID, 
since we cannot have a missing value for the column header.

```{r}
gene_names <- rows_metadata |>
  mutate(gene = case_when(
    is.na(gene_symbol) ~ ensembl_gene_id,
    !is.na(gene_symbol) ~ str_c(ensembl_gene_id, "_", gene_symbol))) |>
  select(row_num, gene)
```

We turn the matrix around (samples as rows, genes as columns) with a long
pivot followed by a wide pivot. Column `X1` is the gene row number. The
sample columns are `X2`, `X3`, ..., so sample number `column_num` in
`columns_metadata` is the column number minus 1.

```{r}
expression_wide <- expression_matrix |>
  rename(row_num = X1) |>
  left_join(gene_names,
            by = "row_num") |>
  select(-row_num) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("X"),
               names_to = "column_num",
               values_to = "rpkm") |>
  mutate(column_num = str_remove(column_num, "X"),
         column_num = as.numeric(column_num) - 1) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = gene,
              values_from = rpkm)
```

Joining onto `columns_metadata` puts the sample information first.

```{r}
dat_load <- columns_metadata |>
  left_join(expression_wide,
            by = "column_num")

dat_load |>
  select(1:12)
```

## Write data

```{r}
dat_load |>
  write_tsv(file = here("data/01_dat_load.tsv"))
```
